Changelog

Source: NEWS.md

NADIA 0.99.2

Changes made in response to the Bioconductor review (#186).

Significant user-visible changes

  • NADIA no longer sets the random seed; call set.seed() to reproduce results. The seed arguments have been removed, and pattern_profiler_analysis() replaces seeds with n_starts.
  • 61 helper functions used by the metric and benchmarking functions are no longer exported (reducing the number of exported functions from 111 to 50; 51 with the new preprocess_se()). The high-level functions continue to return all previously available outputs.
  • Protein score columns are PG.Score and PG.Score.RunWise_* in every format, instead of PG.Cscore; the original report metric is preserved in the nadia_labels attribute. Older tables and .nadia files can still be loaded.
  • imp_method = "missForest" now treats proteins as observations, as MsCoreUtils does; observations = "samples" retains the orientation used by NAguideR.
  • imp_method = "nbavg" has been removed, and bpca no longer accepts nPcs.

New features

  • process_proteomics() accepts a SummarizedExperiment through the new import function preprocess_se().
  • export_format also applies to the exported matrices.

Dependencies

  • limma, rrcovNA, pROC and MsCoreUtils move to Imports; highcharter, reactable and paletteer move to Suggests; readr is removed. The availability of each suggested package is checked before use, and an installation command is provided if it is missing.
  • Imputation methods zero, min, with, MinDet, MinProb, QRILC, bpca and missForest, along with vsn normalization, now use MsCoreUtils and produce the same results as before.

Bug fixes

  • Batch correction with protected covariates no longer discards measured values: proteins that cannot be corrected while protecting the covariates receive batch-only correction.
  • All plotting functions resolve palettes consistently; an unknown palette name raises an error.
  • Heatmaps accept partial row annotations, preserve condition colors in comparison-specific heatmaps and no longer modify ComplexHeatmap options.
  • Interactive tables on the same page no longer interfere with each other. Excel export preserves text that starts with digits, and condition names containing underscores are accepted.
  • Exported tables quote fields that contain tabs, newlines or quotes.
  • .nadia files restore the processing result exactly, except for the precision weights produced by limpa.
  • im_prepare_se() accepts norm_method = "log2".
  • A Parquet export without arrow fails before the analysis starts.

NADIA 0.99.0

Initial Bioconductor submission.

  • Import of protein-level reports from Spectronaut (preprocess_spectronaut()), DIA-NN (preprocess_diann()) and Proteome Discoverer, including both TMT (preprocess_tmt()) and label-free (preprocess_lfq()).
  • process_proteomics() runs normalization (13 methods), optional batch correction, imputation (20 methods, including the two-stage MAR/MNAR combo strategy) and differential abundance analysis with limma or limpa.
  • Each protein’s missingness is reported alongside its fold change: across the experiment, within the comparison and within each condition (MissGlobal, MissComp, MissCND1, MissCND2).
  • Evaluation of normalization and imputation methods (normalization_metrics(), imputation_metrics()) and spike-in benchmarking with OpDEA metrics (benchmarking_proteomics(), benchmarking_multiple()).
  • Soft clustering of abundance profiles with Mfuzz (pattern_profiler_analysis()).
  • Interactive and static figures (volcano plots, boxplots, PCA plots, heatmaps and cluster profiles) and interactive result tables.
  • write_nadia() and read_nadia() save and load a complete analysis in a single DuckDB file.
  • Example dataset nadia_dia and trimmed example reports in inst/extdata/.
